jobs_results.description:
About Engine
Engine is the AI-native platform for intelligent travel. For a decade, Engine has built the proprietary technology and supply behind modern business travel, serving over 40,000 customers and nearly 2 million travelers, along with leading travel and AI companies that build on Engine's infrastructure. One system powers business travel, group travel, human agents, and AI agents.

That work has earned Engine recognition as TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), a spot on Inc.'s Power Partners list (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020–2026).

We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar.

Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us.

Your Mission

We’re looking for an Analytics Manager to lead product analytics for our Pricing & Supply teams. This group powers Engine-only rates, our marketplace coverage and how competitive we are. Its decisions move conversion, margin and customer value every day.

This is a product-first leadership role. You and your team will sit inside product pods as thought partners who shape the roadmap, not as a reporting function waiting on tickets. Experimentation is how we make decisions here: you’ll set the standard for how Pricing & Supply tests, measures and learns. You’ll also take on technically demanding problems such as pricing models, demand and elasticity analysis, and causal questions that a simple A/B test can’t answer.

You don’t need a pricing or supply background. You do need to be excited by hard marketplace problems and by building a team that turns them into better products and better decisions. Join us in reshaping how businesses experience travel.

What You’ll Do

Lead, coach and grow a team of about 5 analysts embedded with Pricing, Supply and Content.
Act as a strategic partner to product and business leaders. Shape roadmaps, challenge assumptions and bring forward opportunities nobody asked you to find.
Own the experimentation program for Pricing & Supply: test design, power and sample sizing, guardrail metrics, readouts, and the judgment to know when not to test.
Go beyond basic A/B testing when the problem needs it. Use holdouts, quasi-experiments, difference-in-differences, or matching when randomization isn’t possible or two-week tests miss the real effect.
Lead analysis on pricing and marketplace dynamics, including price elasticity, demand and conversion modeling, rate competitiveness, supplier performance, margin tradeoffs and customer segmentation.
Partner with Pricing to evaluate, stress-test and improve the models that drive Engine-only rates. Make sure the team understands what drives model outputs, not just what the outputs are.
Set a high bar for rigor: clear metric definitions, sound statistics, honest uncertainty, and storytelling that leads to action.
Push back with evidence when a decision, launch or metric doesn’t hold up, and coach your team to do the same.
Work with Data Engineering and Analytics Engineering to strengthen data foundations, canonical metrics and self-serve tools, so your team spends its time on high-leverage work.
Model an AI-forward way of working and build team habits for using AI tools well, including verifying what they produce.

What You’ll Bring to Engine
Required

7+ years in product analytics, product data science, or a closely related role, embedded with product and engineering teams.
3+ years managing and developing analysts or data scientists, with a track record of hiring and retaining strong talent.
Deep experimentation experience: designing, running and interpreting A/B tests at scale, plus a working knowledge of causal inference methods for cases where clean randomization isn’t available.
Strong statistical foundations, including regression, hypothesis testing, and variance reduction or similar techniques. Comfortable working with and pressure-testing predictive or pricing models.
Expert SQL on large, complex datasets, and proficiency in Python or R for analysis and modeling.
A product-first mindset: you start with the customer, the business and the decision at hand, not the warehouse.
Clear examples of insights you or your team started that changed a roadmap, launch or pricing decision, with measurable impact.
The conviction to hold a well-reasoned position with senior stakeholders, and the communication skills to influence technical and non-technical audiences alike.

Preferred

Experience with pricing, revenue management, marketplaces, supply or inventory, or other two-sided businesses.
Experience with demand forecasting, price elasticity, or optimization problems.
B2B experimentation experience, such as account-level randomization, small samples, or multi-user accounts.
Experience building an analytics or experimentation function from an early stage: telemetry, canonical metrics, testing infrastructure.
Familiarity with modern data tools such as Snowflake, dbt, Looker, Hex, or experimentation platforms.
Experience in travel, hospitality, fintech, or other high-transaction businesses.
Compensation
Our compensation packages are based on several factors, including your experience, expertise, and location. In addition to a competitive base salary, all roles receive equity. Depending on the role, total compensation may also include an annual bonus. Your recruiter will share your complete compensation package as you move through the process.

Location: Remote or Nashville, TN

Status: Full-Time

Compensation: Competitive salary + bonus, full benefits, unlimited PTO, and a seat at one of the coolest campfires in food

About KindlingKindling is a Nashville-based snack company making protein pretzels for people who’d rather be outside. We pair the crunch of a classic pretzel with nutrient-dense protein, fiber, and whole grains, in craveable flavors like Sea Salt, Dill Pickle, Honey Mustard, Garlic Parmesan, and Churro.

We’re a young, fast-growing brand in natural, conventional, club, and e-commerce channels, built by a founding team that has scaled a nationally recognized better-for-you brand before. We give 1% of revenue to the outdoor spaces where communities thrive and play, through the Kindling Impact Foundation.

Our mission: Every moment outside matters. We’re here to feed it.

About the RoleWe have more data than we have hours to read it. SPINS, Circana, retailer portals, distributor feeds, shelf data: it’s all coming in. We need someone who can turn it into a clear answer: where we’re winning, where we’re leaking, and how sales can activate against it.

This is an analyst seat with a sales-support job. You’ll help build the story behind every line review, sell-in, and promo decision, and you’ll sit close to the sales team, not off in a reporting corner.

Please note: this role will report to the Head of Sales.

What You’ll DoTurn data into direction˃ Own weekly and monthly performance reporting across SPINS (via Bedrock), Circana (Costco), and retailer portals: Walmart Luminate, Target, and Albertsons.

˃ Diagnose the “why” behind the numbers, covering velocity, distribution, pricing, promo lift, and share against the category and competitors.

˃ Spot risks and opportunities before we’re asked about them: underperforming stores, voids, and distribution gaps worth chasing.

˃ Use distributor and shelf data (UNFI and KeHE via Treator) to connect what ships with what sells.

Arm the sales team˃ Build category review, line review, and sell-in decks that give buyers a reason to say yes.

˃ Run promo post-evaluations and trade ROI so we spend where it works.

˃ Support Costco rotation planning and read results: demo lift, sell-through, and the case for the next rotation.

˃ Partner on trade and deduction visibility as we roll out Confido.

˃ Field ad-hoc questions from sales, brokers, and leadership. Fast and accurate beats perfect and late.

Build the system˃ Help shape how we use Bedrock, Treator, Confido, Dirty Hands, and whatever comes next.

˃ Create repeatable dashboards and scorecards so the basics run themselves.

˃ Use AI tools to speed up analysis and free up time for thinking.

What You’ll BringMust have˃ [2–4 / 5+] years in CPG sales analytics, category management, or insights, on the brand side, at a broker, or at a data provider.

˃ Deep, hands-on SPINS experience. Circana or Nielsen is a plus.

˃ Experience in at least one retailer portal (Luminate, Target, Albertsons, or similar).

˃ Strong Excel. You build the model; you don’t just open it.

˃ The ability to turn a pile of numbers into three sentences a buyer or CEO will act on.

˃ Comfort learning new tools quickly. We’ll teach you our stack, and you’ll probably end up teaching us.

Nice to have˃ Natural/specialty and conventional channel experience.

˃ Club channel, especially Costco.

˃ Experience with trade spend or deduction platforms.

˃ Power BI, Tableau, or similar.

˃ Experience at an early-stage or high-growth brand.

What Success Looks LikeIn your first 90 days˃ Weekly reporting is running across all data sources.

˃ You own the next major line review deck.

˃ You’ve found at least one opportunity we weren’t seeing.

In your first 12 months˃ Sales walks into every buyer meeting with a data story.

˃ Promo decisions are backed by post-evals.

˃ The reporting runs itself, so you’re spending time on insight, not assembly.

The Culture We're BuildingWe’re not just stacking resumes—we’re gathering the kind of people you’d want around a campfire. Curious minds. Brave creatives. Whole humans.

The Heartbeat – How we show up

Be a Steady Flame – Transparent, consistent, and always lit with integrity.

Invite Others to the Campfire – Every voice matters. Roast marshmallows, not ideas.

Kindle Your Passions – Burnout isn’t a badge of honor. We value balance, walks in the woods, and midday creative breakthroughs.

The Output – What we expect

Defend Our Den – Care about the craft. Own your wins and your misses.

Seek Higher Ground – Challenge assumptions. Expand your view. Ask why (then why again).

Take Swift Action – Light the match. Follow the spark. Adjust as you go.
